title: Will this desk fit? Scanning with an iPhone

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Will this desk fit in the room? Most people grab a tape measure. Antoine took out his iPhone and scanned the whole apartment with LiDAR.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The whole apartment? Was that for floor plans?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Not at all. In January 2024 they used Rhino on iPhone, not for permit drawings, just to settle layout questions before buying furniture.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It's about relative confidence. Hallway width, closet depth, whether a 60 inch TV wall is real or wishful thinking. They checked the TV wall against a tape measure afterward, and it was within a few centimeters. Good enough for furniture.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What went wrong on day one?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Glossy and dark surfaces. Glass and the TV screen left holes. Clutter turns chairs and boxes into bumpy walls. And long loops drift, so in the narrow hallway he walked it twice and closed the loop at the front door.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: How do you know when a patch is bad?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The live mesh is the quality gate. Grey holes mean walk that patch again, not export and hope.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Furniture stayed in place on purpose. Beds and dressers get lumpy, which is fine if you only need clearance paths. For clean walls, empty the room first. They learned that the hard way on a closet door swing.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So when does this beat full CAD?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Early layout questions. If the scan survives one furniture decision, it already paid for the hour. The full write-up has the limits table and the export stills.
